title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-ryan-murphy
content:
PR: refactor kv-cache + batching (draft) — notes to self / review checklist

TL;DR:
- Large refactor touching kv cache eviction + continuous batching scheduler. Goal: reduce p99 token generation latency under mixed workloads while improving cache hit rate.
- Biggest risks: subtle race on async eviction, perf regression from locking, and metrics mismatch after moving to per-shard caches.

Quick summary of changed areas:
- cache/sharded_kv_cache.py: introduced ShardedKVCache, per-GPU shards, async evict thread removed in favor of cooperative eviction during request completion.
- scheduler/batcher.py: changed batching window logic to prefer deadline-based flush for low-latency requests; added wake-up heuristic to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- runtime/lock_manager.py: new RWLock around hot-keys; replaced global cache lock in several hot paths.
- metrics: cache.hit/miss counters moved to per-shard tags; added cache.evictions and cache.eviction_reasons gauge.

Immediate concerns to validate in review:
- Race condition on eviction: earlier async thread guaranteed single-threaded evict; now eviction can run on any request completion path. Need to ensure two concurrent evictions don't double-free entries.
  - grep for `_evict_entry` usages — ensure attempts to evict check "is_valid" and use atomic compare-and-swap on slot state.
  - add unit test that creates 2k concurrent completions that collide on same key and assert no double-free / stale pointer.

- Locking overhead: RWLock introduced fine-grained locking but used in hot allocation path in cache.get_or_insert. Benchmark microbench: 
  - baseline get_or_insert (old) p50 120ns, p99 3.1ms on micro-bench with 128 tokens workload.
  - current change: p50 180ns, p99 4.9ms — that p99 jump could matter under tight SLOs; need to measure in end-to-end perf harness.
  - TODO: run `bench/kv_cache_microbench.py --workers 64 --ops 1e6` and attach results to PR.

- Batching semantics: deadline-based flush looks good for latency requests but may reduce batching efficiency for throughput-heavy routes (embeddings/long-context chat).
  - Add opt-in config param: `batching.prefer_latency` default false for per-route config so we don't change global behavior.
  - Validate autoscaler interplay: smaller batch sizes could increase tokens/sec and trigger scaling decisions. Add simulation run.

Testing checklist:
- [ ] unit tests for concurrent eviction (new test file tests/test_kv_cache_eviction_race.py)
- [ ] microbench results included in PR description (bench logs)
- [ ] e2e perf run on staging with mixed workload (chat+embeddings) comparing p50/p95/p99 token latency and tokens/sec by model
- [ ] integration test for metrics reconciliation: ensure total cache hits + misses == requests seen for sample interval and no metric duplication after per-shard tagging
- [ ] add canary rollout plan in PR (start with 5% traffic on dedicated cluster)

Review notes / suggestions for author:
- prefer clear invariants: add docstring at top of ShardedKVCache describing concurrency model, allowed concurrent ops, and where CAS is used. Right now assumptions are spread across methods.
- switch `RWLock` implementation to the optimized one in runtime/lock_utils which uses futex on linux — current implementation is generic python lock with borrows; that will add overhead in C-extension hot paths.
- consider keeping async evict thread but make it cooperative: evict thread drains low-priority queue while regular completions can do immediate eviction only for small number of entries (fast path). That reduces worst-case contention on eviction.
- metrics: ensure per-shard tags include shard_id and region for cross-cluster aggregation; update metrics ingestion lambda to sum across shard tags (add migration note).

Minor code nits:
- cache/sharded_kv_cache.py: avoid using broad except: pass — replace with specific exceptions and log at debug level.
- scheduler/batcher.py: use monotonic() for timeouts (avoid system clock jumps).
- runtime/lock_manager.py: remove leftover `print` debug and replace with logger.debug.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- Add a periodic scrubber that runs at low priority to remove long-stale entries to reduce eviction spikes during traffic surges.
- Add an internal doc page (Confluence) describing batching heuristics so product/infra teams can tune per-route flags without code changes. Link: confluence placeholder.
- Run a 24hr soak on dedicated cluster with 1.5x traffic to observe steady-state eviction rates and memory churn.

Questions for the author (call out in PR):
- Why move to per-shard metrics now? Is there a query use-case that required this for debugging, or just performance isolation?
- Was the async evict thread removed for correctness or perf? If perf, can we reintroduce it as optional config?
- Where is the canonical place for batching config (route vs model vs global)? Let's explicit in code comments and doc.

Copy of quick TODOs for me before approving:
- [ ] reproduce p99 regression locally with bench harness
- [ ] request author to add concurrent eviction unit test
- [ ] verify canary rollout steps in PR description and add monitoring dashboards (cache.evictions, p99 latency, batch-size distribution)
- [ ] sanity check memory accounting after per-shard split (could double-count if accounting not careful)
- [ ] once tests pass, approve with request to gate `prefer_latency` behind feature flag for 2 weeks

Scratch / thoughts (brain dump):
- If p99 is mostly from locking tail latencies, maybe switch to optimistic path: try no-lock fast path read, then fallback to lock for writes — similar to seqlock pattern. Worth prototyping.
- Eviction double-free: maybe safer to mark entries tombstone and let scrubber clear them; avoids racing frees but increases short-term memory. Trade-offs.
- Could add lightweight per-key generation counters to detect stale references (cheap compare), simple but adds some memory per entry.

End notes: this PR is conceptually good and addresses a real issue with global cache hotspots, but we must be conservative — the cache is central to p99 SLOs. If the author can add the requested tests and microbench logs and gate the latency-first heuristic behind a route config/feature flag, I'm inclined to approve after green e2e perf and canary plan.

-- Ryan
